title: Optimize Conductor 4.0 beta release notes and migration guide
author: Priya Ramakrishnan
content:
> **Archived 2028-09-15:** this page is superseded by "Optimize Conductor 4.0 release notes and migration guide" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

These notes cover the Optimize Conductor 4.0 beta: what is new, API and console changes, expected SLO and cost effects, the recommended migration and rollout steps, and known issues with rollback guidance. The 4.0 beta introduces a multi-tenant optimization engine, tighter coupling with the Fidelity Advisor, and kernel-aware scheduling aimed at lowering per-token cost without degrading observed fidelity.

Release goals

- Lower average per-token inference cost for mixed conversational traffic (beta measurements: 15–35%, depending on traffic shape).
- Allow the Optimize Advisor and serving runtime to negotiate fidelity live for SLO-aware routing.
- Give Conductor 2.x/3.x customers a telemetry-first migration path with minimal disruption.
- Keep SDKs and partner integrations working through a stable API plus a migration shim.

Highlights

1) Multi-tenant optimization engine
- Federated optimizer holding per-tenant batching and caching policies behind a global, capacity-aware admission controller.
- Improves cross-tenant utilization and reduces cold starts for low-volume tenants.

2) Kernel-aware scheduling and quantization profiles
- The scheduler reads model architecture and hardware kernel fingerprints to pick quantization and execution paths per batch, with automatic fallback to safe paths under load.

3) Fidelity Advisor v2 integration
- Per-request fidelity negotiation with the serving runtime, evaluated against live telemetry and historical customer thresholds. Decisions are auditable and feed crediting adjustments.

4) Hybrid KV-prefetch cache coordinator
- A local-prefetch proxy plus cloud-coordinated KV eviction to cut repeated KV misses in session-heavy chat workloads.

5) Telemetry and cost normalization
- New per-route cost attribution fields (cost_estimate, cost_adjuster_id).
- Streaming telemetry schema v3.

6) Console and API
- New UI with per-tenant policy editor, rollout simulator and migration dashboard.
- API: /optimize/v4/policies, /optimize/v4/migrate, /optimize/v4/simulate

Compatibility and deprecations

- SDKs calling /optimize/v3 are routed through a compatibility shim that keeps prior semantics for 6 months post-release. We recommend migrating to v4 within 60 days to get the full performance benefit.
- The legacy batch policy fields 'batch_target_ms' and 'kv_strategy: legacy' are deprecated; a removal date will be announced at GA.

SLO and performance notes

- Latency: steady-state median generation latency is unchanged; p95 can improve on quantized paths but may rise ~5–10% during migration while batchers warm.
- Cost: 15–35% savings observed in beta for mixed chat + embeddings workloads, sensitive to session affinity and prompt length.
- Telemetry: ingestion should reach 99.9% delivery; customers using fidelity negotiation should keep telemetry propagation under <750ms to hold tight latency SLOs.

Compatibility matrix (summary)

- Conductor 2.x -> 4.0: migration shim required; staged canary rollout recommended.
- Conductor 3.0 -> 4.0: direct upgrade supported after running the playbook compatibility tests.

Migration plan

Ownership: product -> release manager; eng-platform -> rollout; eng-serving-runtime -> runtime compatibility; customer-success -> customer comms.

1) Preparation (2 weeks before canary)
- Pick tenants for staged rollout, starting with a 5–10% traffic slice.
- Confirm telemetry forwarding >= 99% and /v1/health checks on local-prefetch proxies.
- Run the preflight simulator (POST /optimize/v4/simulate) and record the cost_estimate delta.

2) Canary (1 week)
- Deploy 4.0 to one region for non-critical tenants only.
- Watch p50/p95 latency, KV miss rate, policy decision errors and fidelity negotiation failures.
- Leave the compatibility shim on for SDKs still hitting /v3.

3) Gradual rollout (2–6 weeks)
- Step traffic 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%, waiting at least 24 hours of stable telemetry between steps.
- Compare cost and quality metrics to baseline.

4) Post-rollout verification (2 weeks)
- Run fidelity regression suites and gather customer-reported regressions.
- Turn off the compatibility shim after 14 days with no critical regressions.

Checklist

- [ ] Preflight simulation run and cost_estimate baseline captured.
- [ ] Customer SDKs updated to v4, or compat fallback accepted.
- [ ] Telemetry schema v3 ingestion enabled for the tenant.
- [ ] KMS/HSM policies validated for encrypted KV prefetch state.
- [ ] Canary window agreed with customer success for high-value accounts.
- [ ] Rollback points recorded (cluster snapshots, config versions).

API examples

- POST /optimize/v4/policies
  payload: {"tenant_id":"t-123","policy":{"fidelity_target":"balanced","batch_budget_ms":60}}
- POST /optimize/v4/migrate
  payload: {"tenant_id":"t-123","target_version":"4.0","dry_run":true}
- POST /optimize/v4/simulate
  payload: {"traffic_profile":"conversational-heavy","seed":42}

Internal CLI: rwdctl optimize migrate --tenant t-123 --target 4.0 --dry-run

Observability

Schema v3 adds:
- cost_estimate (float): optimizer-estimated USD per 1000 tokens
- cost_adjuster_id (string): applied cost normalization rule
- fidelity_decision_id (string): link to Fidelity Advisor decision traces

Suggested alerts
- fidelity.negotiation.failures > 1% in 5m -> Sev2 (eng-serving-runtime)
- kv.miss_rate > 2x baseline in 10m -> Sev2 (eng-platform)
- telemetry.ingestion.failures > 0.1% in 15m -> Sev1 (eng-sre)

Quality and evaluation

- Regression harness at tests/regression/optimize_v4/ with conversational-heavy, short-prompt-burst, embedding-only and mixed-transactional traffic shapes.
- Track response_consistency, hallucination_rate (where available), latency_p95 and per_token_cost.

Known issues

- Heavy partitioning can raise tail latency by up to 40% in the KV-prefetch coordinator until evictions settle; set prefetch:fallback_to_local = true as a workaround.
- Edge model variants with custom CUDA kernels may not benefit from kernel-aware scheduling yet.
- The migration dashboard may show stale cost deltas for low-traffic tenants; use the simulate endpoint instead.

Rollback

1) Pause rollout and roll back policies via the /optimize/v4/policies rollback API.
2) If the regression persists, restore the previous conductor image from cluster snapshot and disable the multi-tenant optimizer flag.
3) Notify customer-success and schedule a hotfix window.

Security and compliance

- Prefetch cache state persisted to disk must be encrypted with customer KMS keys for restricted-confidentiality customers.
- All fidelity negotiation decisions go to the audit log stream, retained per the customer's compliance tier.

Customer communication

- Send the migration playbook and preflight checklist 10 business days before migration.
- Offer enterprise customers an optional 30-minute technical review during canary.

Appendix A: Compat shim behavior

- Maps legacy batch_target_ms to batch_budget_ms with normalization factor 0.75.
- Disables kernel-aware scheduling for shimmed requests.
- Returns header X-Optimize-Deprecation: v3-compat; replacement: /optimize/v4
